feed.title: NPR Topics: Health
feed.subtitle: Comprehensive health news from NPR. Follow for updates on medical research, wellness trends, public health policy, patient care and healthcare systems.

entry.title: Some people with meat allergies from alpha-gal syndrome turn to exotic alternatives
entry.summary: People with alpha-gal syndrome can have allergic reactions to meat from mammals. Many of those affected change their diets to eat other proteins.

entry.title: The Ebola outbreak is breaking records -- and just marked a grim milestone
entry.summary: The current outbreak, first identified in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has now counted 10,000 patients and has spread with great speed. How can it be stopped?

entry.title: A 'Green Army' is out to thwart El Niño flooding
entry.summary: In Nairobi, a city prone to floods, workers in the "Green Army" are making preparations to prevent disaster when El Niño arrives.

entry.title: Special ed diaries: Teachers tell NPR about their most joyous, most difficult moments
entry.summary: What makes special education teaching jobs so hard to fill? NPR set out to find some answers by talking to more than a dozen teachers who do this work every day.

entry.title: Merck's melanoma vaccine trial shows reduced recurrence or death from skin cancer
entry.summary: Merck presented its mRNA melanoma vaccine trial data at a European cancer conference this weekend. Results are promising: The vaccine reduces recurrence and death alongside an immunotherapy drug.

entry.title: Some people with meat allergies from alpha-gal syndrome turn to exotic alternatives
entry.summary: People with Alpha-Gal Syndrome can have allergic reactions to meat from mammals. Many of those affected change their diets to eat other proteins.

entry.title: U.S. measles cases more than double what they were last year as outbreak spreads
entry.summary: Pennsylvania is the worst hit state, with at least 1,338 cases of measles confirmed in 44 counties so far this year, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health.

entry.title: What people aged 50 and older need to know about flu shots
entry.summary: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe asks Dr. Ann Falsey of the University of Rochester Medical School about flu shots for people aged 50 and older.

entry.title: This College of Magic turns ordinary kids into cool magicians
entry.summary: The students, many from marginalized communities, learn to conjure up candy, do card tricks — and face the world with a confident, creative and resilient mindset.

entry.title: More dads taking paid family leave for a new baby, sometimes as much as moms are
entry.summary: The U.S. has no national law for paid parental leave. But in states that do, more dads are using the benefit, sometimes more than moms. The change comes as Americans say having kids is unaffordable.
